name: GLOW Wednesday Warfare

matches.note: Koyomoto used Walavan's own size against him, evading his attacks with speed before winning by pinfall with a hurracanrana.
A one-sided main event brawl fought mostly outside the ring with found weapons; Davies won by pinfall with a Death Valley Driver and left with Knight's own trademark headband.

note: Opens on a debut match and a debut tag match not structured here (neither opponent is separately notable in this record), then the two matches above, before a commentary recap of the promotion's own second pay-per-view and a look ahead to the coming weekend's card.

evidence.source: The following week's own broadcast, in its own recap segment.
evidence.note: Dark Justice opened the card with a pinfall win over Gods Justice.

evidence.source: The following week's own broadcast, in its own recap segment.
evidence.note: "Spirit Warrior" Jin Tao won by disqualification over the much larger Death Incarnate after a third wrestler's interference, meant to help Tao, instead helped Incarnate; the recap frames the two interferers as newly allied.

evidence.source: The following week's own broadcast, in its own recap segment.
evidence.note: "The Cobra" Marco Carlson beat "The Cornerstone" Jeffrey Drake in a match announced during the week to become the number-one contender for the Northeast Championship.

evidence.source: The following week's own broadcast, in its own recap segment.
evidence.note: The Perfectly Perfect Duo, with manager Sensuous Samantha at ringside, retained the Tag Team Championship over the Sons of Savagery.

evidence.source: The following week's own broadcast, in its own recap segment.
evidence.note: "No Remorse" John Davies beat "Kamikaze" Kris Klepan and Kyle Cross together in a Hardware Store match, finishing with a piledriver through a car's sunroof.

evidence.source: The following week's own broadcast, in its own recap segment.
evidence.note: "The Incomparable" Dylan Rapture beat "Showstopper" Scott Jamison for the Lightheavyweight Championship's own number-one contendership after the Perfectly Perfect Duo and Sensuous Samantha turned on Jamison mid-match.

evidence.source: The following week's own broadcast, in its own recap segment.
evidence.note: King Apples beat Andrew "Flash" Tucker in a no-rules match, then revealed on-air that he, not Tucker's own handler, had been sleeping with the promotion founder's wife, and that she had secretly sold the promotion to him; Apples fired both the founder and Tucker on the spot.

evidence.source: The following week's own broadcast, in its own recap segment.
evidence.note: "Simply the Best" James Pillow retained the Heavyweight Championship over Northeast Champion Victor V. Hill and "Confident" Lawrence Williams in a triple-threat match after Erin McCoys ran in to attack Pillow with a loaded purse and struck Hill instead, letting Pillow steal the pin.
